text:
kevin: Offer accepted — new hire Mira is on H-1B with previous employer and will start 6/1. She has a portability petition receipt (I-797C). Can she start on 6/1 under portability?

tara: Yes, per USCIS portability rules an employee whose employer filed an H-1B transfer and received a receipt can start once the new employer files and they have the receipt notice. We still need to complete Form I-9 and examine acceptable documents.

immigration-bot: I-9 note: employers may accept an unexpired passport plus an H-1B portability receipt (I-797C) for proof of identity and employment authorization ONLY if the employee's current I-94 shows lawful admission. If the I-94 is expired, the employee must present updated arrival evidence.

payroll: Operationally we can onboard Mira on payroll with a 6/1 start date if People Ops receives scans of passport and the I-797C receipt before then. Benefits enrollment follows the standard cutoff (20th for 1st-of-next-month).

tara: Important travel advisory: if Mira leaves the US before she obtains an H-1B visa stamp from a consulate, reentry is not guaranteed on the portability receipt. Recommend avoiding international travel until stamping is confirmed.

kevin: Manager approves 6/1 start contingent on docs. I'll DM Mira to request scans and confirm no travel planned. People Ops to draft a short addendum clarifying start contingent on portability docs.

immigration-bot: If you'd like the two-page H-1B portability quick-guide and I-9 checklist, reply and I'll post it.

kevin: Thanks team — closing loop.
